title: Proof of Value Onboarding Charter
content:
Overview:

This document is the customer-facing charter for the upcoming Proof-of-Value (PoV) engagement with Evergreen Financial (EF). It defines objectives, measurable success criteria, scope, risks, workshop plan, and the evaluation approach we will use to determine whether the engagement meets both Evergreen's product goals and Redwood Inference's viability criteria for a production deployment.

Purpose and high-level objective:
- Give Evergreen a runnable demonstration of Redwood inference in a production-like configuration that validates performance, cost, and integration assumptions for a conversational assistant placed in front of customer account workflows.
- Deliver a concise decision: "Go to pilot (Dedicated)" or "Iterate on model/integration" within four weeks from kick-off.

Primary success criteria (must meet all):
1) Latency: end-to-end P95 response time <= 250ms for single-turn generation at 512 token cap under target load (30 requests/sec sustained during synthetic soak).
2) Accuracy: task-level correct routing rate >= 88% on Evergreen’s curated eval set (50 representative dialogues). Correct routing = assistant choosing the right downstream system or response template.
3) Cost envelope: estimated unit inference cost <= $0.017 per 1k tokens in a Dedicated-like configuration (projected monthly load 2M tokens).
4) Security & data flow: customer-approved data path (either Dedicated or Private) with KMS integration and audit log proof-of-concept for 14 days of retention.
5) Integration: successful end-to-end webhook flow from Redwood -> Evergreen backend with <= 3 integration defects blocking production-like flows (bugs that prevent request/response exchange).

Secondary success criteria (nice-to-have):
- KV cache hit rate > 20% for repeated user prompts (improves cost).
- Smooth streaming enabled for the user-facing demo (no disconnects in 95% of streams).
- Baseline hallucination rate on open-ended prompts < 6% as measured by manual review of 100 sampled responses.

Scope (in-scope):
- Evaluate Redwood hosted and Dedicated configuration performance with Evergreen’s sample traffic shape.
- Instrumentation for token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns using Redwood Console dashboards.
- Basic webhook integration proof-of-concept and sample fallbacks for model throttling.
- Two-day on-site (or remote) hands-on workshop with Evergreen engineering and product stakeholders to configure prompts, integrate webhooks, and run evals.

Non-goals (out-of-scope for this PoV):
- Full enterprise-grade SAML SSO onboarding and long-term SLA contracting.
- Multi-region DR testing, long-term retention/backups beyond the 14-day audit window.
- Production data migration or retroactive user history seeding.

Timeline and milestones (target cadence):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): alignment workshop, roles, and access checklist completed; sample data share initiated.
- Week 1: Redwood environment provisioned (hosted + small Dedicated test pool), integration wiring (webhook + test credentials), baseline latency/throughput smoke tests.
- Week 2: Evaluation harness run against Evergreen eval set; workshop day 1 (prompt engineering + augmentation techniques).
- Week 3: Workshop day 2 (load testing + failure mode/rollback rehearsals); final metric capture and cost projection.
- Week 4: PoV review session and decision; deliverable: concise recommendation memo and next-step roadmap.

Milestone acceptance checkpoints:
- Environment Ready: Redwood API keys and Dedicated test pool available to Evergreen (acceptance = smoke test passes).
- Integration Ready: webhook round-trip and sample webhook-driven action verified (acceptance = 95% success in 100 attempts).
- Evaluation Complete: required metrics collected and recorded in the evaluation sheet (acceptance = all primary metrics measured or explained).

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood Solutions Lead: Ava Patel — overall engagement lead, workshop facilitator, executive summary owner.
- Redwood SRE/Infra: Samir Rao — Dedicated pool provisioning, load-test orchestration, and console dashboards.
- Redwood ML Engineer: Leila Nguyen — evaluation harness, scoring, prompt recipes.
- Evergreen Lead Engineer: Martin Cruz — provide test endpoints, sample dataset, and integration coordination.
- Evergreen Product Owner: Nina Brooks — business acceptance, scenario validation, and final decision sign-off.

Data & access requirements (to be completed in Week 0):
- Evergreen must provide: 1) anonymized sample dialogues (>= 500 utterances), 2) canonical routing labels for 50 eval dialogues, 3) webhook endpoint and test credentials, 4) data retention policy for audit.
- Redwood will request scoped service account and short-term KMS key (or test stub) to validate encrypted payloads.

Workshop agenda (2 days, remote or on-site):
Day 1 (4 hours):
- 00:00–00:20 Introductions, goals, evaluation rubric walkthrough
- 00:20–01:00 Environment tour: Redwood Console, model catalog, and cost panel
- 01:00–02:00 Prompt engineering sessions: templates, tool calling / structured output examples
- 02:00–03:00 Hands-on: wiring Evergreen webhook, test scenario run
- 03:00–04:00 Q&A, next steps, task assignment

Day 2 (4 hours):
- 00:00–01:00 Load testing design and safety controls (throttles, fallback models)
- 01:00–02:00 Soak test: sustained load at 30 req/sec with incremental token sizes
- 02:00–03:00 Failure rehearsal: model fallback, region failover simulation, and rollback plan
- 03:00–04:00 Metric review, decision criteria confirmation, and action items

Evaluation methodology & scoring rubric:
- Each primary criterion is scored pass/fail. Secondary criteria receive a 0–10 score each.
- Overall PoV rating = Pass if all primary criteria pass and average secondary score >= 6.
- Record raw measurement artifacts: Console screenshots (latency over time), cost projection table, and eval harness output CSV.

Acceptance tests (concrete tests to run):
1) Latency soak: synthetic traffic at 30 req/s for 20 minutes, measure P95 and error rate.
2) Routing accuracy: run 50 labeled dialogues through the system; acceptance >=88% correct routing.
3) Webhook stability: 1000 round trips with 95% success.
4) Security check: KMS-encrypted payload round trip and audit event recorded.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customer eval set not representative. Mitigation: capture additional user telemetry and plan a short second-phase eval with broader sample.
- Risk: Dedicated pool not provisioned in time. Mitigation: use hosted fallback with matched model variant and document differences in cost/latency.
- Risk: hallucination / safety issues during demo. Mitigation: enable strict guardrails, response filters, and manual moderation channel for demo sessions.

Communication and reporting:
- Weekly status emails to stakeholders (Ava to lead).
- Daily stand-in Slack thread for rapid troubleshooting: #solutions-pov-evergreen.
- Final memo to include: measured metrics, artifacts, list of open issues, recommended next step (pilot / iterate), and an estimated timeline & cost for pilot.

Deliverables at close of PoV:
- Executive one-page recommendation (decision + rationale).
- Raw eval artifacts: logs, Console screenshots, CSV exports from eval harness.
- Integration runbook (short doc with webhook settings, error codes, and rollback steps).
- Follow-up roadmap if Go-to-Pilot selected: required infra, SSO/entitlements, SLA terms to finalize.

Decision criteria and next steps:
- If Pass: Redwood and Evergreen agree to begin a 3-month Dedicated pilot; assign contract owner and target go-live window.
- If Fail: Capture root causes and recommended iterations (model tuning, data collection, or different routing strategy); propose a 6–8 week remediation plan.

Notes & open questions for kickoff (to resolve in Week 0):
- Which Evergreen environment will hold customer PII (staging vs. redacted sample)?
- Preferred cost accounting cadence for the Dedicated estimate (monthly vs. projected Q).
- Approval path for a short-term KMS test key vs. providing access to customer-managed KMS.

Appendix: Quick checklist for Week 0 (tick-box style):
- [ ] NDA / PoV scope signed
- [ ] Account & API keys created for Redwood demo account
- [ ] Dedicated test pool request submitted
- [ ] Sample dialogues + labels uploaded to shared Confluence folder
- [ ] Webhook endpoint and test credentials shared
- [ ] Stakeholders calendar invites scheduled (workshop days)

Prepared by: Ava Patel (Redwood Solutions Engineering)
